---
title: "Package Usage Knowledge"
---

## Scope and source of truth

SCGSim owns reusable **layout/EM** geometry, preparation, execution, resolution,
and report procedure. It does not own component designs, circuit/quantum
runtime, project Notebook placement, or permission to execute a solver.
The package is an independent downstream toolkit, not official gsim.

Usage knowledge is authored in the documentation pages below. The offline
bundle is a build-generated view of those same sources, bound to the installed
distribution version and content digests. It is not a second editable recipe
set. Reading installed knowledge must not import a solver, start a session,
access a source checkout, or require MCP. MCP may expose these installed
resources but does not own or rewrite their meaning.

This knowledge-distribution surface is **CONVERGING**. Capability descriptions
are not scientific acceptance, solver convergence, or stable-release claims.

## Build and installed discovery

The build-only `_build_backend.py` wraps setuptools' `build_sdist` and
`build_wheel` hooks and generates
`scgsim/_agent_knowledge/manifest.json` plus the declared QMD resources. The
manifest implements `scq-mcp-akb-1.0` (schema `"1.0"`): exact distribution
version, stable resource IDs, titles/kinds/summaries/status, source-relative
provenance, SHA-256 of each source/resource, and a canonical `bundle_id`.
QMD is preserved as UTF-8 source text; it is never executed during generation.

Run `uv build --no-sources` from the package repository to build the sdist and
its wheel. The sdist includes generated bundle data, this build hook and the
canonical public sources; rebuilding it requires neither a checkout nor a
solver import. Standard Python build dependencies must already be available
for a network-disabled build. Generated files are ignored locally and must
not be edited as documentation authority. Repeated builds of the same version
and sources produce identical manifest/resource bytes; archive timestamps are
not part of the bundle identity.

Install the **built wheel**, not an editable checkout, in the consumer/MCP
Python environment. MCP discovers files through
`importlib.metadata.distribution("scgsim")`, the installed file list and
`locate_file`; it does not import SCGSim to discover knowledge. Every bundled
file has an ordinary wheel `RECORD` hash and size. The reader verifies those
along with manifest identity, installed version and resource hashes.

An absent bundle, unsupported editable installation, missing resource, version
mismatch, unsafe path or byte drift is an explicit unavailable/error result,
not permission to fall back to a workspace, web recipe or solver import.
MCP search/read may enforce its documented transport size limits; these are
not scientific eligibility rules. No MCP dependency, producer entry point,
runtime parser or solver capability is added by this distribution mechanism.

## Canonical resource inventory

| Reader task | Editable package authority | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Choose a supported backend | [Backend support](backend-support.qmd) | Implemented candidate versus planned or excluded; not inferred from a namespace. |
| Supply geometry semantics | [SGB geometry](geometry-sgb.qmd) | PDK fabrication facts plus source-authored component nets/ports/topology. |
| Organize stage-local calls | [Notebook UX](notebook-ux.qmd) | Package call order and immutable runs; consumer repository owns Notebook files and pairing. |
| Configure Palace | [Palace + SGB](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd) | Electrostatic/Eigenmode, Route A/B, terminals, physical/exterior ground, native masked Surface EPR. |
| Configure AEDT | [AEDT families](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd) | Typed family-specific model/setup controls, native exports and readback. |
| Prepare or execute | [Execution profiles](execution-profiles.qmd) | Explicit preparation versus launch; copied inputs and exact compatibility evidence. |
| Interpret a run | [Report model](report-model.qmd) | Strict resolution, failed/partial inspection, selected-snapshot integrity, solver-specific quantities. |
| Inspect geometry | [Geometry preview](geometry-preview.qmd) | Semantic mapping and preview availability, not solver evidence. |
| Preserve evidence | [Provenance](provenance.qmd) | Receipt/hash identity and public/private data boundaries. |

The inventory deliberately excludes project component notebooks, runs, meshes,
native projects, screenshots, machine configuration, and maintainer routing.
Existing paired documentation/Notebook sources and Human-executed outputs are
not converted or overwritten by knowledge generation.

## Prerequisites by operation

| Operation | Python dependencies | External requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Read this installed knowledge | Installed SCGSim distribution; Python 3.12 | None; no network or solver import. |
| Palace geometry-to-handoff and Plotly reports | `scgsim[palace]` | Gmsh's platform libraries for meshing; a Palace executable is **not** a pip extra. |
| Execute a Palace handoff | Same exact SCGSim installation plus the handoff's runtime environment | Compatible Palace and launch/MPI environment; Slurm only for a Slurm profile. |
| AEDT typed preparation and results | `scgsim[aedt]` (PyAEDT 1.3.0 and GDS support) | Native execution requires AEDT 2024.2 and an available license. Preparation does not open Desktop. |
| Geometry previews | `scgsim[visualization]` plus the selected backend's dependencies | Working headless rendering; AEDT project readback additionally requires AEDT/license. |

`--all-extras` is an installation choice, not permission to execute a solver
and not proof that native libraries, binaries, rendering, or licenses exist.
Compare the installed distribution version with the consumer's selected exact
dependency. Do not silently replace it with a newer checkout.

## Procedure migration boundary

The public procedure formerly distributed through layout-simulation Notebook
profiles is represented here only where SCGSim owns the meaning:

- geometry/stack before Surface-EPR configuration, mesh controls before mesh,
  numerical controls before config, config before handoff;
- exact-net terminals and grounds, authored port sheets, and typed AEDT
  families instead of Notebook-local semantic reconstruction;
- explicit execution, fresh output identity, sealed native readback, and
  strict-versus-partial result interpretation;
- distinct physics and cost surfaces, units, mode/excitation/port ordering,
  and no local CSV parser, failure classifier, or solver-config patch;
- read-only Notebook review for those calls and boundaries, not a formatting
  result presented as scientific validation.

Project-specific headings, file placement, pairing, execution permissions,
cell IDs, and preservation of existing outputs remain with the consuming
repository. Legacy central authoring tools remain in place during migration;
this package does not remove them. Their general solver recipes do not create
APIs missing from the installed package: for example, the current AEDT runtime
does not expose a retained-project continuation API. See each backend's
explicit exclusions rather than constructing a Notebook-local substitute.
